bugs.creator: kevinushey
bugs.summary: use `getOption("INSTALL_opts")` as default for INSTALL_opts argument to install.packages()

comments.creator: kevinushey
comments.text:
Often, one needs to customize how packages are installed -- e.g. via configure flags, configure arguments, or arguments passed to `R CMD INSTALL` itself.

`install.packages()` has the signature:

```
install.packages(pkgs, lib, repos = getOption("repos"),
                 contriburl = contrib.url(repos, type),
                 method, available = NULL, destdir = NULL,
                 dependencies = NA, type = getOption("pkgType"),
                 configure.args = getOption("configure.args"),
                 configure.vars = getOption("configure.vars"),
                 clean = FALSE, Ncpus = getOption("Ncpus", 1L),
                 verbose = getOption("verbose"),
                 libs_only = FALSE, INSTALL_opts, quiet = FALSE,
                 keep_outputs = FALSE, ...)
```
And so the value of `getOption("configure.args")` as a default for its `configure.args` argument, and similarly for `configure.vars`.

My wishlist item: could R also accept `getOption("INSTALL_opts")` as a set of defaults to use for the `INSTALL_opts` argument? With a similar convention around allowing a named list of arguments, to allow customization based on the name of the package being installed.

(One motivation: when using R with the Windows Subsystem for Linux, package installations can fail in some cases with staged installs / use of lockfiles during install. Having a mechanism for the user to control the defaults here would help.)
